title: Ease into prayer without shame
whyMatters: Prayer sits at the center of Muslim life, and learning it is genuinely hard at the start. Easing in gives you a way to keep going without treating every mistake as a reason to stop.

exactActions.text: Learn the shape before the details
subSteps: Learn the names of the five prayers and roughly when they fall.
Watch or read one simple guide to the movements.
Keep a short reference beside you while you practice.
Choose the prayer you are most likely to catch every day.
Get that one steady before you add another.
If you miss it, pick things up at the next prayer instead of spiralling.

exactActions.text: Use what you know while you learn the Arabic
subSteps: Start memorizing Al-Fatiha a line at a time.
Read from paper or your phone while you learn if you need to.
Ask a teacher what the minimum recitation is for a beginner in your situation.
Do not measure your faith by how neat your prayer looks.
Every attempt makes the next one less strange.
Ask Allah to make prayer beloved and steady for you.

timeEstimate: 1 to 2 weeks for a first routine

obstacles.solution: Missing prayers while you are learning is common. Set reminders, start with one anchor prayer, and ask a qualified teacher how to make up what you missed in your situation.
Learning in private is completely fine. Allah sees the effort, and every Muslim you know had to learn these words and movements from scratch.

tinyVersion: Pick one prayer to protect today, even if you need a guide open beside you.
unlocksNext: Once you have a way in, the full prayer step stops looking like a wall.

commonQuestions.problem: Can I pray while reading from a guide?
commonQuestions.solution: Many beginners do exactly that. Ask a local teacher about the details, especially once you are ready to tidy up your prayer.

contextNotes.title: At work or school
contextNotes.body: Work out which quiet spaces you can use and which prayer windows are realistic. If you need an accommodation, ask calmly and keep the request practical.
